name: All the Stations of the Slow River
description: A quiet, devastating holographic drama following a Tier 2 water-transit worker, Adaeze Morrow-Krishnamurthy, as she ferries cargo across the reclaimed Lake Michigan channels over the course of a single season. The film's holographic rendering is deliberately low-resolution in its interiors — a formal choice that makes the vast exterior lake sequences feel shocking in their clarity. It won the Meridian Independent Film Accord's highest prize and was quietly acquired by a Vantablack subsidiary, which has never re-released it.
cultural_impact: All the Stations of the Slow River remains a touchstone for GLMZ independent cinema precisely because of its inaccessibility — the Vantablack acquisition effectively buried it, making it a symbol of corporate suppression of working-class art.
story_hooks: Director Obinna-Castillo wants his film back and has found a legal loophole in the acquisition contract — he needs people to help him retrieve the master from a Vantablack archive facility.
A Tier 1 pirate broadcaster has been running degraded copies of the film; Vantablack has sent a cease-and-desist team that seems disproportionately aggressive for a decade-old indie.
Adaeze Morrow-Krishnamurthy, the film's lead, has discovered something in the Lake Michigan channels that mirrors the film's fictional subplot about submerged infrastructure — and she's terrified.
